source.title: SensorLM: Learning the Language of Wearable Sensors
source.authors: Yu-Wei Zhang; Kumar Ayush; Siyuan Qiao; A. Heydari; Girish Narayanswamy; Maxwell A. Xu; Ahmed A. Metwally; Shawn Xu; Jake Garrison; X. Xu; Tim Althoff; Yun Liu; Pushmeet Kohli; Jie-Ning Zhan; Mark Malhotra; Shwetak N. Patel; Cecilia Mascolo; Xin Liu; D. Mcduff; Yu-Zhe Yang

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some text and a figure in the appendix are garbled, but the scaling results relevant here are also described in text.
record.tranche_reason: It examines scaling of downstream AUROC in sensor-language models, a different setting and measure from held-out language-model cross-entropy; this bears on downstream predictability but does not test the original loss laws.
record.gate_note: The study reports a scaling analysis of zero-shot activity AUROC as compute, data size, and model size vary. The scaling figures also contain plotted results that are not recoverable as exact values from the provided text; only results stated explicitly in the text are recorded.
record.test_reason: It reports how zero-shot activity AUROC changes as compute, data size and model size grow in a sensor-language model (contrastive plus captioning). That is a new setting with a result on downstream scaling (V6). It fits no power law and measures no held-out loss, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested. T3 fits better than T2, because the study's question is its own model family, not a new method for the original question.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. Authors say SensorLM shows 'consistent and predictable' scaling with compute, data and model size, with data gains diminishing beyond 12M hours and undertrained XL underperforming. They take this as showing scaling laws apply to sensor-language modeling, though they fit no law.
record.recipe_differences: This is sensor-language pretraining evaluated mainly by zero-shot activity AUROC, not language-model pretraining evaluated by held-out cross-entropy loss. Its scaling analysis does not fit power laws or optimize a compute-budget allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with training compute: SensorLM-XL underperforms when undertrained. Data gains diminish beyond 12 million hours.
record.problems: The scaling results relevant here are mostly qualitative; apart from the SensorLM-B compute example, exact AUROC values for the scaling sweeps are not stated in the text. No power-law fit, loss measurement, or predictive extrapolation is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 8 includes plotted results across compute, data size, and model size, but the provided text does not make their exact values reliably recoverable. Only the results described explicitly in Section 5.2 and Appendix C.1 are recorded.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss is measured and no power law is fitted.
No fit on small runs is extrapolated to larger runs.
No compute-optimal split of parameters versus data is studied.
Depth and width are not varied at a fixed parameter count.
The modality is non-text, but neither a power-law form nor a loss is measured, so whether the same form holds is untested.
Downstream performance is not related to pretraining loss, no predictive fit or out-of-sample forecast is made, and only zero-shot activity AUROC is scaled.
Fitting choices and exponents are not compared.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. The evidence is weak: zero-shot downstream AUROC on one task family, read from a Pareto-front figure (Fig. 8) whose values are unrecoverable, with only one numeric pair in the text. The 'scaling laws' language is loose; no power law, exponent or loss curve is reported. Row r4 should not be used as a challenge.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining cross-entropy loss is measured.
No small-run fit is used to predict larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute optimization of parameter and token allocation is reported.
The study does not compare depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
It studies sensor-language models, but does not test whether the same power-law form holds for held-out loss; it reports downstream AUROC trends instead.
The study evaluates zero-shot activity AUROC, not downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss, and does not fit a predictor or report out-of-sample forecasts.
No comparison of fit choices, exponents, or departures from a power-law loss curve is reported.

rows.subject: SensorLM-B
rows.operation_detail: Varied training steps and compute; reported zero-shot activity AUROC.
rows.note: The text presents this as an example of performance improvement with increased training compute.
rows.check: Only two compute points are stated in the text (0.66 at 17.4 TPU hours, 0.75 at 174 TPU hours, 1k to 10k steps). The rise is monotonic, but no fit or forecast backs 'predictable'.

rows.subject: SensorLM models (model not specified for this result)
rows.operation_detail: Expanded the amount of pretraining data and reported zero-shot activity recognition performance.
rows.value: Performance gains diminish beyond 12 million hours; exact AUROC values not stated.
rows.note: The study says expanding data yields gains, especially for larger models, but gains saturate beyond the stated data amount.
rows.check: The subject is vague: the text says gains diminish 'for certain models' beyond 12M hours, without naming them. No AUROC values are given; the saturation is stated only in words.

rows.subject: SensorLM family (SensorLM-S, SensorLM-B, SensorLM-L, SensorLM-XL)
rows.size_stated: sensor encoders have 3M, 114M, 404M, and 1.27B parameters, respectively
rows.operation_detail: Compared zero-shot activity recognition performance across model sizes.
rows.value: Larger models generally outperform smaller counterparts when adequately trained; exact AUROC values not stated.
rows.locator: Section 5.2, Scaling Laws; Appendix C.1, Model scaling
rows.note: The statement is a family-level comparison; the text does not give separate numerical AUROC values for each model.
rows.check: Qualitative only: 'larger models generally outperform' when adequately trained. Per-model AUROC is only in Figure 8 and cannot be read.

rows.subject: SensorLM-XL
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated a large model at low training compute.
rows.value: Underperforms due to undertraining; exact AUROC value not stated.
rows.locator: Section 5.2, Scaling Laws; Appendix C.1, Model scaling
rows.note: The paper explicitly contrasts this low-compute result with the larger model's advantage when sufficiently trained.
rows.check: Marking this 'reversed' is wrong. The undertrained XL losing at low compute is the compute-bottlenecked regime, which the scaling claims exclude, and the authors call it consistent with scaling laws. It does not show downstream performance failing to improve with scale.

relationships.condition: SensorLM compute sweep (SensorLM-B) and model-size comparison when adequately trained
relationships.reason: Zero-shot activity AUROC rises from 0.66 to 0.75 with 10x compute (r1), and larger models beat smaller ones given enough compute and data (r3). The evidence is monotonic trends, not a fitted law.
relationships.display_finding: Zero-shot activity AUROC increased from 0.66 to 0.75 with 10× compute, and larger models performed better given sufficient compute and data.

relationships.condition: Data scaling beyond 12 million hours, for some models
relationships.reason: Gains saturate beyond 12M hours of data for certain models (r2), so downstream improvement with data is not sustained across the whole tested range.
relationships.display_finding: Downstream gains saturated beyond 12 million hours for some models.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.reason: Data gains diminish beyond 12 million hours, and the undertrained XL model underperforms at low compute; the trend is not uniform across these settings (r2, r4).
